newsitem.title: GERMANY: German IBIS DAX ends the day practically unmoved.
newsitem.headline: German IBIS DAX ends the day practically unmoved.

text.p: Germany's IBIS DAX index ended the day practically unchanged on Wednesday, with little new data around to move the market in any significant direction.
The IBIS DAX index, which tracks electronic trade in German shares, ended at 3,651.59 points, down four points or 0.11 percent, while the June DAX future was down seven points at 3,655.50 points.
Earlier the DAX index ended floor trade one percent higher at 3,661.84 points. The DAX was higher as it tracked gains from the previous evening's electronic trade.
Traders said that there was upside in the IBIS DAX index to around 3,700 points in the short-term, but that gains would be capped at that level in the current jittery atmosphere.

"My mid-term target is 4,000 points, but I don't think that will happen until there is a decision on petroleum tax. 3,700 will act as a cap, but then again, predictions keep getting broken these days," a Frankfurt trader said.

In a series of statements over the morning, both Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said the German government and the Bundesbank had reached a way of proceeding on a planned revaluation of central bank assets.
He also said that he and Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer would do their best to have windfall funds created by the revaluation transferred to Bonn from 1998 and not earlier.
The decision had a fairly neutral effect on shares, despite the fact that uncertainty about the future of European currency union had translated into negative sentiment in the equity market of late.
Germany's large utilities enjoyed a cyclical upturn for much of the day, but then pared gains over the day.
Viag AG ended up four marks, or half a percent, at 784 marks, while Veba was up 83 pfennigs, or 0.85 percent at 98.05 marks.
In contrast, RWE AG ended the day down 1.05 marks, or 1.40 percent, at 74.40 marks.

Shares in Deutsche Telekom AG were higher after Wolfgang Schaeuble, parliamentary leader of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), said the sale of the government stake in the company would be done in a way that would not upset shares.
Telekom shares ended up 25 pfennigs, or 0.65 percent, at 38.47 marks.
Privatisation talk also boosted airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG which ended up 35 pfennigs, or 1.19 percent, at 29.60 marks.
